Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I followed indications i got from the emails sent to me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, the international relations office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very! i was able to attend all those i wanted to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take some time to figure out if the courses and their schedules don't overlap before you register.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved my courses there, the teaching is excellent!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Three on bachelor level
Three on master lives

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More old-school, a bigger student-teacher distance, but i love it. I think the courses generally are much more innovative and thrilling there. One feels that they renew the courses regularly. In Copenhagen university one has the feeling that they have taught the same for ten years.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Two one contemporary philosophy (on Nietzsche, and Foucault and Ricouer)
Two metaphysics (on being and god, and on phenomenology of spirit of hegel)
One common course on the notion of exteriority
one on history of modern philosophy (phil. of language in the 17th and 18th century).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, but the one on Foucault and ricoueur. It was bit superficial the seminars: a lot of historical details without not so much conceptual in depth.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I haven't attended any, but i think the erasmus organised might be fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Whatever they want:) There are loads of possibilities, great museums, cinemas, theaters - you name it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to find some local friends

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to approach people, it's almost always rewarding! Many people there also need somebody to talk to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any specific, just mostly the language barrier some times. But its fun to learn another language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The studying culture around the libraries. I love to study there side by side with so many others. One feels that there is a small community. It's beautiful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be afraid to ask or reach out, both students and teachers are open and nice.
Look out for activities or something if you feel alone. I think it's a great way to meet others. 
I myself found the library a good way to meet people. Many of the same people go there every day and in the end it's easy to talk to them and hangout together. It can be more difficult with the courses you take, because its almost never the same people in the all of the classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that i can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my french! And meeting people that like studying as much as i do:)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking french in the beginning - the spoken language is very different, but people are nice and patient! Don't be afraid to just do it, even make faults, you figure out that people understand you and that gives confidence.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
